result.summary: Validates the options parameter in the sendall RPC using strict type checking, rejecting any unrecognized keys. It also removes the unused solving_data option from sendall documentation and argument parsing, bringing option validation in line with RPCs like send and fundrawtransaction.
result.problem: sendall silently ignores unknown or misspelled option keys. A caller who typos an option like inputs as input will unintentionally spend all available wallet UTXOs instead of the specified subset, or inadvertently broadcast a transaction if psbt or add_to_wallet is misspelled.
evidence: PR description: 'sendall silently ignores unknown keys in its options object, including misspelled ones: input instead of inputs spends all available UTXOs rather than the given ones, and a misspelled add_to_wallet or psbt can broadcast a transaction the caller asked not to broadcast.'
Commit b517c3d915 notes that strict checking occurs before fee arguments are merged into options so that misspelled fee estimation options like estimate_mode are caught immediately.
result.changed_since_previous: Diff provided; the patch matches the earlier description without changes.
result.card: Reject unrecognized keys in the options dictionary of the sendall RPC rather than silently ignoring them, and remove the unused solving_data option. Callers making typos in option names currently face unintended wallet behavior, such as spending all wallet UTXOs if inputs is misspelled, or broadcasting an unintended transaction if psbt or add_to_wallet is mistyped. The change aligns sendall with existing strict option parsing in RPCs like send, fundrawtransaction, and bumpfee.

risk.why: Stricter argument validation on an existing RPC method can fail external scripts or integrations that previously passed unrecognized options.
